mainTopic: Changing charity and synagogue donations; ערכין, vows, and damages of a גוסס and a יוצא ליהרג
overview: The amud opens by asking how רבי ינאי could borrow charity money and repay it. The answer is that his borrowing actually helped the poor. A ברייתא then teaches that a Jew's donated מנורה or נר for a בית הכנסת may not be changed. רבי יוחנן limits this to voluntary uses, so changing it for a מצוה is allowed. A non-Jew's donation is different: it may not be changed while his name is remembered, since he might protest. The story of שעזרק's lamp shows the sages disagreeing over whether that worry applied to him. Next comes a new משנה about a גוסס and a יוצא ליהרג, discussing vows, ערכין, and liability for damage. The גמרא uses ״כׇּל חֵרֶם לֹא יִפָּדֶה״ to explain both sides of the ערכין dispute. It then shows that the real argument between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי is about damage. רב יוסף and רבא each give a reason for that argument, and some place their dispute on a different ברייתא.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי ינאי's borrowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that charity money in the collector's hands may not be changed, since רבי ינאי used to borrow from it and pay it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי ינאי used to borrow charity money and repay it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the earlier rule that once charity money reaches the גבאי it may not be changed. It points to רבי ינאי, who borrowed from the charity funds and later paid them back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If charity money in the collector's hands could never be changed, borrowing it should be forbidden. Yet a great sage like רבי ינאי did exactly that. So the rule seems too strict.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word for a challenge
But look! It brings a fact that seems to contradict the rule
Borrowed
Repaid

phrases.english: Is that so?
But Rabbi Yannai would borrow and repay!
phrases.notes: רבי ינאי was a charity collector, so he borrowed from the charity money in his care.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַבִּי יַנַּאי יָזֵיף וּפָרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule stated just before this passage, that charity money in the גבאי's hands may not be changed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that once charity money reaches the גבאי it is forbidden to change it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real-life case: רבי ינאי borrowed charity money and repaid it, showing that changing its use was allowed.

steps.title: רבי ינאי's borrowing helped the poor
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי's case is different because his borrowing actually brought in more money for the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי is different, because it was good for the poor: the longer he left the fund empty, the more he pushed people to give, and he brought in more for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ינאי's case is a special exception. His borrowing benefited the poor, so it does not contradict the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the charity fund looked empty, רבי ינאי could press people to donate more. In the end the poor got more money than before. So the general rule stays, and his case is an exception because it worked in the poor's favor.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different. Sets apart a case as an exception
It is good or pleasing for them
Poor people
Presses or pushes others to act, here to give charity

steps.whatToRemember: Charity money in the גבאי's hands may not be changed, but borrowing that ends up helping the poor, like רבי ינאי did, is an exception.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai is different,
since it is good for the poor,
for the longer he delays repaying,
the more he presses people to give, and he brings them more.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (an exception with a special reason)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ינאי's borrowing shows that charity money may generally be changed.
steps.terutzMaskana: His case is an exception because it benefited the poor; the general rule stays in place.

steps.title: A donated lamp may not be changed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a Jew donates a מנורה or נר to a בית הכנסת, it may not be changed to another use.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if a Jew donated a candelabrum or a lamp to the synagogue, it is forbidden to change it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on a similar topic: donations to a בית הכנסת. A Jew's donated מנורה or נר may not be put to a different use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like charity money, a gift given for a specific purpose should stay with that purpose. The ברייתא does not yet say whether this applies to every new use, which the next steps will discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
Donated as a free-will gift
Candelabrum
Lamp
To change it, to use it for a different purpose

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A Jew who donated a candelabrum
or a lamp to the synagogue,
it is forbidden to change it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִתְנַדֵּב מְנוֹרָה אוֹ נֵר לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a related topic: changing donations given to a בית הכנסת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew's donated מנורה or נר for a בית הכנסת may not be changed to another use.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא: no change for any purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא thought the ban on changing the donation applies even when the new use is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא thought to say: it makes no difference whether the change is for a voluntary use or for a מצוה use.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא gives his first understanding of the ברייתא: the donation may never be changed, even for a מצוה. This sets up the next step, where his view will be corrected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said simply 'forbidden to change it' without limits. רבי חייא בר אבא reads that as a total ban. The word סבר hints that this view will not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say. Often a first idea that is later corrected
There is no difference
A voluntary, non-מצוה matter
A matter involving a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: סבר does not introduce the final halacha. It is רבי חייא בר אבא's first assumption, and the next step corrects it.

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְמֵימָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba thought to say:
there is no difference whether for a voluntary matter
or for a מצוה matter.
phrases.notes: He means it is forbidden to change the donation either way.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְמֵימָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets how far the ברייתא in Step 3 goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Initial assumption: the donated item may not be changed for any purpose, voluntary or מצוה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן permits change for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי reports that רבי יוחנן limited the ברייתא to voluntary uses; for a מצוה use, changing the donation is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי said to him: this is what רבי יוחנן said. The ban was taught only for a voluntary use, but for a מצוה use it is permitted to change it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אמי rejects רבי חייא בר אבא's total ban by quoting רבי יוחנן. The ban applies only to changing the donation for a non-מצוה use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase לא שנו אלא narrows the ברייתא. Changing the donation to another מצוה use is permitted, and only voluntary uses are forbidden. This replaces רבי חייא בר אבא's first assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of. Limits a teaching to a narrower case
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, a donated מנורה or נר may not be changed for a voluntary use, but may be changed for a מצוה use.

phrases.english: Rav Ami said to him:
This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
They taught this only for a voluntary matter,
but for a מצוה matter it is permitted to change it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַמֵּי: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the assumption of Step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the ban covers מצוה uses too.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן taught that the ברייתא only refers to voluntary uses.

steps.title: Proof from a non-Jew's donated lamp
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support for רבי יוחנן's view from his ruling about a non-Jew's donation: forbidden to change while the donor is remembered, permitted once he is forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: We know this from what רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if a non-Jew donated a candelabrum or a lamp to the synagogue, as long as the owner's name is not forgotten it is forbidden to change it; once the owner's name is forgotten it is permitted to change it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up רב אמי's report of רבי יוחנן. It quotes רבי יוחנן's ruling about a non-Jew's donation, which will be analyzed in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling makes a difference based on whether the non-Jewish donor is still remembered. The proof will come from asking what kind of change this ruling is talking about. Here the source is only being laid out.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that he said. Introduces a source used as proof
A non-Jew
Was forgotten, literally sank away
The name of its owner, here the donor

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: We know this from what Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
A non-Jew who donated a candelabrum
or a lamp to the synagogue,
as long as its owner's name has not been forgotten,
it is forbidden to change it;
once its owner's name has been forgotten,
it is permitted to change it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רבי יוחנן's view stated in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that changing a donation for a מצוה use is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling (via רבי אסי) about a non-Jew's donated מנורה or נר.

steps.title: What kind of change is the non-Jew ruling about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what use the non-Jew ruling refers to, and shows it cannot mean a voluntary use, since then even a Jew's donation would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what purpose? If you say for a voluntary use, why mention a non-Jew in particular? Even a Jew's donation is the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins working out the proof by asking what kind of change the non-Jew ruling means. It rules out a voluntary use, setting up the conclusion that the ruling must be about a מצוה use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already said a Jew's donation may not be changed for a voluntary use. So if the non-Jew ruling were about voluntary use, there would be no reason to single out a non-Jew. This pushes toward reading it as a מצוה use, which would show that a Jew's donation may be changed for a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? Asks what case or purpose is meant
If you say. Introduces a possible reading to test
Why specifically this case? Asks why this detail was chosen
Even

phrases.english: For what purpose?
phrases.notes: He means: for what kind of new use is changing it forbidden before the donor is forgotten?

phrases.english: If you say for a voluntary matter,
why specifically a non-Jew?
Even a Jew too!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא in Step 3 already forbade changing a Jew's donation for a voluntary use.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי? אִילֵימָא לִדְבַר הָרְשׁוּת, מַאי אִירְיָא גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the source brought in Step 6 to draw out the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What type of change (voluntary or מצוה) the non-Jew ruling refers to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Voluntary use is ruled out, because a Jew's donation already has that ban. Step 8 gives the answer: the ruling is about a מצוה use.

steps.title: The non-Jew's ruling is about a מצוה use, because he would protest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's ruling about a גוי's donation refers to changing it for a מצוה. It is forbidden only because a גוי would complain, while a Jew would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ruling is about changing it for a מצוה. The reason it is forbidden is that a גוי complains. A Jew does not complain, so for him it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 7. The ruling about a גוי's donation must be talking about a מצוה use, and the reason is that a גוי would protest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 showed the ruling cannot be about a voluntary use, because then even a Jew's donation would be forbidden. So it must be about a מצוה use. A Jew's donation may be changed for a מצוה, since a Jew would not mind. A גוי might shout, 'Where is my lamp?', so we wait until his name is forgotten. This supports רבי יוחנן's distinction between voluntary uses and מצוה uses.

keyTerms.meaning: for a מצוה purpose
cries out, protests loudly
it is perfectly fine, permitted

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew's donation may be changed for a מצוה. A גוי's donation may be changed for a מצוה only after his name is forgotten, because until then he might protest.
steps.confusionAlert: The problem with the גוי is not that a מצוה use is wrong. The only issue is his likely complaint, which ends once he is forgotten.

phrases.english: Rather, it is about changing it for a מצוה matter,
and the reason is that it is a non-Jew, who screams in protest,
but a Jew, who does not scream,
it is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לִדְבַר מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7 by settling on the only remaining option, a מצוה use.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of use the ruling about a גוי's donation is talking about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מצוה use. It is forbidden only for a גוי, who would protest. A Jew would not protest, so his donation may be changed.

steps.title: The story of the lamp donated by שעזרק
steps.stepSummary: A non-Jewish merchant, שעזרק, donated a lamp to רב יהודה's בית הכנסת. Someone changed its use and someone else got upset. The versions differ on who did what.
steps.simpleTranslation: שעזרק the Arab donated a lamp to רב יהודה's בית הכנסת. רחבה changed it and רבא got upset. Some say רבא changed it and רחבה got upset. Others say the attendants of פומבדיתא changed it, and both רחבה and רבה got upset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that matches the rule about a גוי's donation. It gives three versions of who changed the lamp and who objected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact case from Step 8: a גוי donated a lamp, and it was changed before he was forgotten. The sages disagreed about whether that was allowed. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: a lamp or candelabrum
a synagogue (בית הכנסת)
became upset, was strict about it
attendants or officials of the community

phrases.english: Sha'azrak the Arab merchant
donated a lamp
to the synagogue of Rav Yehuda.
Rachava changed its use, and Rava got upset.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: שַׁנְּיֵיהּ רָבָא וְאִיקְּפֵד רַחֲבָא,
phrases.english: Some say: Rava changed it, and Rachava got upset.
And some say: the attendants of Pumbedita changed it,
and Rachava got upset, and Rabba got upset.
phrases.notes: Watch the spelling: this is רבה, a different sage from רבא earlier in the story.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁעַזְרַק טַיָּיעָא אִינַּדַּב שְׁרָגָא לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case of the rule from Step 8 about changing a גוי's donation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A real dispute arose over changing a lamp a גוי had donated, while he was still remembered.

steps.title: Why one side changed the lamp and the other objected
steps.stepSummary: The one who changed the lamp thought שעזרק was rarely around, so he would not protest. The one who objected thought he might still show up sometimes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who changed it held that שעזרק was not usually around. The one who got upset held that sometimes he happens to come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of each side in the story of שעזרק's lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on the rule from Step 8: a גוי's donation may not be changed while he might protest. They disagree only about the facts. One side says this donor was rarely in town, so there was no real worry. The other side says he could still visit and complain.

keyTerms.meaning: is not commonly found, rarely around
sometimes he happens to come

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute in the story is not about the rule itself. It is about whether this particular donor was still likely to come and protest.

phrases.english: The one who changed it holds
that he is not commonly around,
phrases.notes: "He" is שעזרק, the donor, who was not often in town.

phrases.english: and the one who got upset holds
sometimes he happens to come.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּשַׁנְּיֵיהּ סָבַר דְּלָא שְׁכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the disagreement in the story of Step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Everyone accepts the rule that a גוי's donation may not be changed while he might protest. The argument was only over whether this donor was likely to come back.

steps.title: New משנה: a dying person and one going out to be executed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a גוסס and a person going out to be executed cannot be the subject of a vow of value or of ערכין. רבי חנינא בן עקביא allows ערכין. רבי יוסי says such a person can himself vow, make ערכין, and be מקדיש, and is liable if he causes damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who is dying, and a person going out to be executed, cannot be vowed on and cannot be valuated. רבי חנינא בן עקביא says: he can be valuated, because his value is fixed. רבי יוסי says: he can vow, make a valuation, and consecrate, and if he causes damage he must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins here. It discusses whether people about to die can be the subject of vows about their worth, and what such people can do themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדר of value depends on what the person would be worth if sold. Someone about to die has no such value. A ערך is a fixed amount set by the Torah by age and gender, so רבי חנינא בן עקביא says it still applies. רבי יוסי adds that such a person can still act: he can make vows, valuations, and consecrations, and he must pay for damage he causes.

keyTerms.meaning: a person in his final moments of life
one being taken out to be executed after a court sentence
is the subject of a vow of his market value ("his value is on me")
is the subject of a ערך, the fixed Torah amount
his amount is fixed, set by the Torah
consecrates property to the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up נידר and נערך. נידר is about the person's market value, which a dying person lacks. נערך is about the Torah's fixed amount, which does not depend on his condition.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who is dying and one who is going out to be executed
is neither vowed upon nor valuated.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא אוֹמֵר: נֶעֱרָךְ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Akavya says: he is valuated,
because his amount is fixed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: נוֹדֵר וּמַעֲרִיךְ וּמַקְדִּישׁ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: he vows, valuates, and consecrates,
phrases.notes: Here the condemned man is the one doing the action, not the one being vowed on.

phrases.english: and if he causes damage, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַגּוֹסֵס וְהַיּוֹצֵא לֵיהָרֵג לֹא נִידָּר וְלֹא נֶעֱרָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the discussion of donations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוסס and one going out to be executed are not נידר and not נערך. רבי חנינא בן עקביא says they are נערך. רבי יוסי says they can vow, valuate, and consecrate, and are liable for damage.

steps.title: Why can't a person going to be executed be valuated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the reasons for the גוסס and for the vow of a יוצא ליהרג, but asks why a יוצא ליהרג cannot be valuated.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: It makes sense that a dying person cannot be the subject of a vow, because he has no money value. It also makes sense that he cannot be valuated, because he cannot be stood up before the כהן and valued. But a person going out to be executed? It makes sense that he cannot be the subject of a vow, because he has no money value. But why can't he be valuated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. It finds a reason for every ruling except one: why a יוצא ליהרג cannot be valuated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow of 'his value' depends on market price, and nobody would buy a man about to die, so no vow works on him. ערכין is a fixed amount set by the תורה based on age and gender, not on market price. The גוסס is excluded because the פסוק requires the person to be 'stood' before the כהן. But a יוצא ליהרג can stand, so the reason for his exclusion is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense; it accepts one point in order to question another
Someone who has a money value (a price on the market)
Being stood before the כהן and then valued; the תורה requires both for ערכין
A person on his way to be executed by בית דין
Why?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up a vow of 'his value' (נדר דמים), which depends on market price, with ערכין, which is a fixed amount from the תורה. The whole question here depends on keeping these two apart.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Granted, a dying person is not the subject of a vow
because he has no money value
and he is not valuated
because he cannot be stood up and valued
phrases.notes: This refers to ויקרא 27:8, where the person is 'set before the כהן' to be valued. A dying person cannot stand.

phrases.english: But one going out to be executed:
granted, he is not the subject of a vow
because he has no money value
but that he is not valuated, why not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא גּוֹסֵס לֹא נִידָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reason that a יוצא ליהרג cannot be valuated, even though ערכין is a fixed sum and he is able to stand.

steps.title: A פסוק teaches that one sentenced to death has no ערכין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״כׇּל חֵרֶם לֹא יִפָּדֶה״ that a יוצא ליהרג who says 'my ערך is upon me' has said nothing. ״מִן הָאָדָם״ limits this to after his sentence is final.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that if a person going out to be executed says, 'My valuation is upon me,' he has said nothing? The פסוק says: 'Anything doomed shall not be redeemed.' Might you think this applies even before his sentence is final? The פסוק says: 'Of men,' meaning not all men.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. It brings a פסוק showing that a יוצא ליהרג cannot be valuated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'חרם' in this פסוק as a person doomed to die, and 'cannot be redeemed' as meaning no ערך can be paid for him. So the exclusion comes from a פסוק, not from logic. The word ״מִן״ ('of' men) limits the rule: it applies only once his sentence has been decided, not before.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asks for a source)
The פסוק teaches
Here, a person doomed to die
Might you think... (sets up an idea that the פסוק will reject)
His sentence has been finally decided

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the exclusion of a יוצא ליהרג from ערכין is a rule of the תורה, and it starts only once his verdict is final.

phrases.english: As it is taught: From where do we know that one going out to be executed
who said, 'My valuation is upon me'
has not said anything?
The פסוק says: 'Anything doomed shall not be redeemed.'
Might you think this applies even before his sentence is final?
The פסוק says: 'Of men'
and not all men.
phrases.notes: The little word 'of' means only some people are included: those whose sentence is already final.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מִנַּיִן הַיּוֹצֵא לֵיהָרֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with a source from a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם לֹא יִפָּדֶה״ teaches that a person condemned to death has no ערך. ״מִן הָאָדָם״ limits this to after his verdict is final.

steps.title: How does רבי חנינא בן עקביא use this פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי חנינא בן עקביא holds that a יוצא ליהרג is valuated, what does he learn from ״כׇּל חֵרֶם״?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי חנינא בן עקביא, who says that he is valuated because his value is fixed, what does he do with this phrase 'anything doomed'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the dissenting opinion in the משנה. It asks what רבי חנינא בן עקביא does with the פסוק that was just used to exclude a יוצא ליהרג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן עקביא says ערכין works for a יוצא ליהרג because the amount is fixed by the תורה. So he cannot be using ״כׇּל חֵרֶם״ to exclude him. Every phrase in the תורה must teach something, so the גמרא asks what this one teaches according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: His value is fixed (set by the תורה, not by the market)
What does he do with it? (what lesson does he learn from this פסוק)

phrases.english: And according to רבי חנינא בן עקביא
who says he is valuated
because his value is fixed
what does he do with this 'anything doomed'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא, דְּאָמַר נֶעֱרָךְ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁדָּמָיו קְצוּבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having used the פסוק for the תנא קמא's view, the גמרא asks how the dissenting view uses it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי חנינא בן עקביא learns from ״כׇּל חֵרֶם לֹא יִפָּדֶה״, since he does not use it to exclude ערכין.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches that no ransom can replace a court's death sentence
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן עקביא uses the פסוק as רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה does: one sentenced to death by a court cannot pay money to be spared, unlike those who die בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He uses it for what a ברייתא teaches. רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: We find that people who deserve death at the hands of Heaven can pay money and be forgiven, as it says, 'If a ransom is laid upon him.' Might you think the same is true for people sentenced to death by a human court? The פסוק says: 'Anything doomed shall not be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חנינא בן עקביא uses the פסוק for a different lesson. A person sentenced to death by בית דין cannot buy his way out with money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the owner of an ox that killed someone, the תורה allows a כופר (ransom) in place of death at the hands of Heaven. We might have thought money could also replace a court execution. The פסוק says 'shall not be redeemed' to teach that it cannot. So for רבי חנינא בן עקביא, 'redeemed' means escaping the death penalty, not paying ערכין.

keyTerms.meaning: People who deserve death at the hands of Heaven, not by a court
Ransom money paid in place of a punishment
He is forgiven (his sin is atoned)
By human hands, meaning execution by בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use ״כׇּל חֵרֶם לֹא יִפָּדֶה״. The תנא קמא learns from it that a יוצא ליהרג has no ערך. רבי חנינא בן עקביא learns from it that a court's death sentence cannot be bought off with money.

phrases.english: For that which is taught:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says:
Since we find that those put to death at the hands of Heaven
can give money and be forgiven
as it says, 'If a ransom is laid upon him'
might you think the same is true for those sentenced by human hands?
The פסוק says: 'Anything doomed shall not be redeemed.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכִדְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by giving the פסוק a different lesson according to רבי חנינא בן עקביא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חנינא בן עקביא uses ״כׇּל חֵרֶם לֹא יִפָּדֶה״ to teach that someone sentenced to death by a court cannot pay a ransom to avoid execution, unlike someone liable to death at the hands of Heaven.

steps.title: Even the lighter death penalties cannot be bought off
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם״ extends the rule to every court death penalty, including the lighter ones whose accidental version can be atoned for.
steps.simpleTranslation: I would only know this about the severe death penalties, whose accidental violation has no atonement. How do I know it also applies to the lighter death penalties, whose accidental violation does have atonement? The verse says: "Any חרם" (״כׇּל חֵרֶם״).
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the ברייתא from Step 15. It uses the word ״כׇּל״ ("any") to widen the rule to all court death penalties.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think only the most severe sins cannot be bought off with money. Those are the sins whose accidental version gets no atonement at all. The word ״כׇּל״ teaches that even the lighter ones, whose accidental version is atoned for, also cannot be paid off once a court has ruled death.

keyTerms.meaning: Severe death penalties, here meaning sins whose accidental version has no atonement
Lighter death penalties, here meaning sins whose accidental version can be atoned for
An accidental, unintentional violation
Atonement
"The verse teaches": introduces the פסוק that proves the point

steps.whatToRemember: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם״ covers every court death penalty, severe or light. None can be exchanged for money.

phrases.english: I would have only the severe death penalties,
whose accidental violation was not given atonement;
the lighter death penalties,
whose accidental violation was given atonement, from where do we know?
The verse says: "Any חרם."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:29. The word "any" is what widens the rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא מִיתוֹת חֲמוּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in Step 15 by widening its rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״כׇּל״ includes the lighter court death penalties, so they also cannot be bought off with money.

steps.title: Does the first opinion really disagree with רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי and asks: did the תנא קמא ever say that a יוצא ליהרג cannot vow or make ערכין?
steps.simpleTranslation: "רבי יוסי says: he vows and makes ערכין, etc." But did the first opinion say that he does not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה. It points out that he seems to be arguing against something the תנא קמא never said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא only spoke about the יוצא ליהרג as the one being valued: others cannot vow his worth or his ערך. He never said this person cannot make vows himself. So what is רבי יוסי arguing about?

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
One who makes a vow to donate someone's worth to the Temple
One who makes a vow of ערכין (a fixed Torah valuation)

steps.confusionAlert: Being the one who is valued is different from being the one who makes the vow. The תנא קמא only ruled on the first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
He vows and makes ערכין, etc.
But does the first opinion say that he does not?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא מִי קָאָמַר דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ״כׇּל חֵרֶם״ discussion and returns to the משנה to examine רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי יוסי disagrees with the תנא קמא about vowing, ערכין, and הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תנא קמא never said a יוצא ליהרג cannot do these things himself, so there seems to be no dispute.

steps.title: The real dispute is about paying for damage
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees he can vow, make ערכין, and be מקדיש. They disagree only about whether he must pay if he causes damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, about vowing, making ערכין, and being מקדיש, everyone agrees. Where they disagree is if he caused damage. The first opinion holds: if he caused damage, he does not have to pay. רבי יוסי holds: if he caused damage, he must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. It says the only real argument is about the last part of רבי יוסי's statement, causing damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vowing, ערכין, and הקדש are agreed on, so רבי יוסי lists them only as background. The new point is damage. The תנא קמא holds that a יוצא ליהרג who damages is not obligated to pay. רבי יוסי holds that he is.

keyTerms.meaning: One who dedicates his property to the Temple
Everyone, meaning all the opinions involved
He caused damage
Payment, compensation

phrases.english: Rather, regarding vowing, making ערכין, and consecrating —
everyone agrees;
where they disagree is if he caused damage.
The first opinion holds:
if he caused damage, he does not have to pay;
phrases.notes: The משנה never states this directly. The גמרא learns it from the fact that only רבי יוסי makes him pay.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei holds:
if he caused damage, he must pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בְּנוֹדֵר וּמַעֲרִיךְ וּמִקַּדִּישׁ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17 by moving the dispute to the damage case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the dispute to a different part of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי disagrees about whether a יוצא ליהרג can vow, make ערכין, or be מקדיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree on those. The only dispute is whether he must pay for damage he causes.

steps.title: What principle is behind the damage dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what underlying issue causes the two opinions to disagree about paying for damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks for the deeper reason behind the argument over damages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally anyone who causes damage must pay. So why would the תנא קמא free a יוצא ליהרג? The גמרא wants the principle that splits them.

keyTerms.meaning: "About what do they disagree?" A request for the root principle of an argument

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dispute identified in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that makes the תנא קמא exempt a יוצא ליהרג from paying for damage while רבי יוסי obligates him.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it depends on collecting an oral loan from heirs
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the dispute is whether a debt with no document (מלוה על פה) can be collected from the heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: They disagree about whether an oral loan can be collected from the heirs. The first opinion holds that an oral loan cannot be collected from the heirs. רבי יוסי holds that an oral loan can be collected from the heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. Paying for damage is like an oral loan, and the argument is whether such a debt can be collected from heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man will soon be executed, so the victim would have to collect from his heirs. A damage debt has no written document, so it is like a מלוה על פה. If such a debt cannot be collected from heirs, the victim gets nothing, as the תנא קמא holds. If it can, he is paid, as רבי יוסי holds.

keyTerms.meaning: An oral loan: a debt with no written document
Collects payment
Heirs

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions agree that a יוצא ליהרג can vow, make ערכין, and be מקדיש. Their dispute about damage comes down to whether a מלוה על פה can be collected from heirs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties a case about a condemned man to a general rule of monetary law about collecting debts from heirs.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
About an oral loan,
whether it is collected from the heirs, they disagree.
phrases.notes: He will be executed soon, so the victim could only collect after his death, from his heirs.

phrases.english: The first opinion holds:

phrases.aramaic: מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין,
phrases.english: an oral loan cannot be collected from the heirs;
and Rabbi Yosei holds:

phrases.aramaic: מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין.
phrases.english: an oral loan can be collected from the heirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: בְּמִלְוָה עַל פֶּה גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by naming the underlying principle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute depends on whether a מלוה על פה can be collected from heirs. The תנא קמא says no, and רבי יוסי says yes.

steps.title: רבא's different explanation: a Torah debt versus a written document
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone agrees a מלוה על פה cannot be collected from heirs. The dispute is whether a debt the Torah creates (מלוה כתובה בתורה) counts like a debt written in a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that an oral loan cannot be collected from the heirs. Here they argue about a debt that is 'written in the Torah.' The תנא קמא thinks such a debt is not like a debt written in a document, so the heirs do not pay. רבי יוסי thinks it is like a debt written in a document, so the heirs pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from step 19 in a new way, disagreeing with רב יוסף's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the argument depends on collecting a מלוה על פה from heirs. רבא says everyone agrees about that, so the argument must be about something else. A debt for damages comes straight from the Torah, and the question is whether that is as strong as a written שטר, which can be collected from heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: A debt 'written in the Torah': a payment the Torah itself requires, like paying for damage
It is treated like a debt written in a document
Everyone agrees
They disagree

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of the dispute. According to רב יוסף, it is about whether an oral loan is collected from heirs. According to רבא, it is about whether a Torah-created debt counts like a written document.

phrases.english: Rava said: Everyone agrees that

phrases.aramaic: מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין,
phrases.english: an oral loan cannot be collected from the heirs,
and here they disagree about a loan written in the Torah.
phrases.notes: He means a payment the Torah itself requires, like paying for damage you caused.

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
a loan written in the Torah
is not like one written in a document,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei holds: it is like one written in a document.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing answer to רב יוסף's explanation in step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason for the dispute about paying for damage
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether a Torah-created debt is treated like a debt written in a שטר. The תנא קמא says no, and רבי יוסי says yes.

steps.title: A second version: the dispute is placed on a different ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some place the רב יוסף and רבא argument on a different ברייתא. That ברייתא says a person going to be executed must pay if he injures others, but others who injure him are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach this argument on a different source: A person going out to be executed who injured others must pay. Others who injured him do not have to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second version. It brings a different ברייתא where the same argument between רב יוסף and רבא will be applied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב יוסף and רבא are not explaining the dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי in the משנה. They are explaining the dispute in this ברייתא, between its first opinion and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The first opinion says the condemned man is liable for damage he causes. People who hurt him are exempt, since he is already considered as good as dead.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it on this source (a second version)
One who is going out to be executed by the court
Injured someone

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on this:
phrases.notes: 'It' means the argument between רב יוסף and רבא you just learned.

phrases.english: One who is going out to be executed,
if he injured others, he is liable;
if others injured him, they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the רב יוסף and רבא dispute onto a different ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condemned person who injures others is liable, and others who injure him are exempt.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: the condemned man is exempt too
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says even the condemned man is exempt if he injures others, because he cannot be brought back to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Even if he injured others, he is exempt, because he cannot be brought back to stand trial in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second opinion that disagrees with the first. It says the condemned man does not pay for damage either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said he is liable. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says he is exempt because his execution cannot be delayed for a new court case. So there is no way to judge him for the damage. This sets up the argument that רב יוסף and רבא will explain in this second version.

keyTerms.meaning: Being brought back to stand before the court for another trial
Exempt, does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is not saying the damage was allowed. He is saying there is no way to take the condemned man to court for it, so in practice he does not pay.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הוּא אִם חָבַל בַּאֲחֵרִים — פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: Even he, if he injured others, is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא נִיתַּן לַחֲזָרַת עֲמִידַת בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: since he cannot be brought back to stand before the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף הוּא אִם חָבַל בַּאֲחֵרִים פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second opinion in the same ברייתא, disagreeing with the first
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condemned man who injures others is exempt, because he cannot be brought back to court for judgment.
